title: Ampe-DB: A Dataset for Human Activity and Interaction Analysis Using the Ghanaian Game Ampe
abstract: arXiv:2610.33130v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Human activity recognition benchmarks underrepresent culturally situated forms of movement and interaction. We introduce Ampe-DB, a multimodal dataset based on Ampe, a traditional Ghanaian game involving coordinated jumping, leg movements, and two-person interaction. It contains 637 canonical clips from 15 participants, with RGB video, two-person pose representations, participant and pair metadata, four-class movement labels, and derived binary movement-relation labels.   We evaluate four-class movement recognition and binary movement-relation classification using three protocols: a duplicate-safe fixed benchmark, four-fold pair-held-out evaluation, and participant-held-out diagnostics for participants with complete class coverage. Baselines comprise a frozen Kinetics-400-pretrained R(2+1)D-18 RGB encoder, a two-layer bidirectional GRU for pose sequences, and validation-selected RGB-pose late fusion. tldr: 该论文推出了Ampe-DB，一个基于加纳传统游戏Ampe的多模态数据集，填补了人类活动识别基准中对文化情境化运动与双人交互形式代表性不足的空白。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Ampe-DB, a multimodal dataset based on the traditional Ghanaian game Ampe, addressing the underrepresentation of culturally situated movement and two-person interaction in human activity recognition benchmarks.
